## Intake review

**Related:** #6528 (the claim-evaporation pattern this feeds — a claimant locked out of its own claim is a direct route to it); filed from an OpenChamber scheduled lane run (lane 262eb403, worker repo-worker-code, 2026-11-08 ~08:40–09:10Z); this issue already carries priority/high + app/fleet.
**Live check:** both observations are from today's live queue (task 12016 claim events 26782–26785; tasks 12832/12851 holding a foreign lane id at 09:07Z); no merged fix found this run.
**Notes / risks:** attribution inverted in both directions means per-lane throughput/cost/abandonment reporting is currently noise — and the checkpoint lockout loses real work. The four-claims-in-seconds sequence suggests the lane stamp is being written by a fan-out the claim path does not own; find the writer before patching the reader.
**Suggested approach:** trace every writer of `tasks.lane_id` and the `claimed` event detail around a single claim, make the atomic claim the only stamper, and add the event-sequence regression test.

— fleet monitor (repo-fleet-monitor), 2026-11-08 10:12 CST run: acceptance criteria appended to the body, labels normalized, `meta/enriched` applied.

## Fresh post-merge recurrence — task 12791

Evidence from OpenChamber session `ses_e5e422dc72affebzR4w41S47IY`, lane `262eb403-3347-4a7c-ba6b-e7bc263ca853`, on `repo-health-code-pilot` (2026-11-09 01:01–01:04Z):

- `repo-queue claim` returned task 12791 for issue #5796; the `claimed` checkpoint succeeded at 01:01:17Z.
- The required follow-up checkpoint later failed with the verbatim broker response: `task 12791 is not claimed by repo-worker-code`.
- The session stopped before creating a worktree or changing repository files. It had posted a pickup note and changed issue labels first.

This occurred after the reported PR #7882 merge at 00:46Z. Please verify whether the running broker has the merged claim-by-id behavior; if so, this is a post-fix recurrence on the live path. No new issue filed because #7598 already tracks the same claim-attribution/ownership failure.

A separate OpenCode session, `ses_e5e422009ffffe7FHvFOanxjKi`, working queue task 12191 / issue #4925, hit the same broker verdict after PR #7882 merged:

`repo-queue: primary queue store failed on /heartbeat (exit 5): heartbeat_task: task 12191 is not claimed by repo-worker-code; switching this work to the GitHub fallback`

The task's lane ledger (row 4006) records `assigned_lane: opencode` and binds `session_id` to this same session. The failed heartbeat occurred about nine minutes after the session started, not after the reported 45-minute claim window. This is distinct from task 12791 / session `ses_e5e422dc72affebzR4w41S47IY` above. Please reconcile both post-merge instances against the live broker/lease history; neither session should be treated as evidence of a successful terminal verb.

issue: #7598

## Criterion-3 claimed-row snapshot audit (2026-11-17T03:27–03:40Z, live)

Live claimed rows sampled across all four pilot queues (10 tasks): 20013, 20022 (code), 18231, 18428, 18486, 18531 (code), 17933, 19434, 19451 (opencode), 17896 (openchamber). Every lane-assignment row reads assigned_lane="direct", assigned_by="repo-worker-code", executed_lane=null while claimed. No row carries a foreign worker or a mismatched assignment.

Muse surface, first-party (this shift, lane any-f): 17 consecutive claims (tasks 12573, 17577, 17584, 17637, 17646, 17655, 17724, 17749, 17594, 18426, 18434, 18444, 18454, 18470, 18492, 18507, 18520) — every checkpoint/complete addressed its claim successfully, zero broker exit-5s, matching task 18528's 16-claim any-h sample. The exit-5 ownership defect has NOT recurred on the Muse path in 33 consecutive sampled claims across two lanes/shifts.

Completion records are thin on both surfaces, though: completed rows keep executed_lane=null (verified on tasks 17594, 17749, 18492, 18507, 18520) because Muse completions pass no --execution — the row never records WHICH lane executed, only assigned_lane="direct".

## Claim-to-complete lane mismatch: reproduced live, pinpointed

First-party repro (2026-11-17, task 20022, still claimed afterwards — the failure is client-side, pre-broker):

    fleet queue complete 20022 --worker repo-worker-code --execution '{"lane":"any-f"}' ...
    -> repo-queue: --execution.lane must be 'opencode' or 'direct'

Root cause: `execution_arg()` in `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/client.rs` (lines ~1432–1446) validates `--execution.lane` against the EXECUTION-ASSIGNMENT vocabulary {"opencode", "direct"} and dies on anything else. A lane id (any-n, any-f) is not in that vocabulary — so the 2026-11-16 session (claim --lane any-n, complete --execution lane=any-n) was rejected for the lane value and only went through with lane="opencode", recording the SURFACE as the executed lane and losing the claiming lane. Two different "lane" vocabularies share one field name: claim `--lane` takes a registry lane id; `--execution.lane` takes an assignment surface.

## Fix spec (remaining work, parked on task 20022)

- Decide the field semantics: `--execution.lane` should record the executing LANE ID; the surface (opencode/direct) already lives in the assignment row's assigned_lane/executed_lane vocabulary and in --platform's family values.
- client.rs: accept a registered lane id in --execution.lane (validate against the lane registry the claim path already uses), or split the keys (lane = lane id, surface = opencode|direct) with the old values mapped for compatibility.
- Broker: on complete, when --execution.lane names the claiming lane, record it (executed_lane or a lane_id stamp on the task row) so a claim-to-complete round trip leaves claim lane == completion lane, per the 2026-11-17 acceptance note.
- Regression test: claim --lane <id> then complete --execution '{"lane":"<id>"}' succeeds and records that lane.

This issue stays open for Drew's close call per the 2026-11-13 reminder; task 20022 is parked with this audit + spec as its remaining work.

🤖 **Agent note** · criterion-3 audit (partial) + pinpoint — task 20022 parked with resume state
- **Agent:** queue worker (repo-worker-code), lane any-h
- **Session / ID:** task 20022 (the criterion-3 audit packet from task 18528's triage)
- **Audit sample (Muse surface, this shift, 2026-11-17):** 24 consecutive claims by lane any-h across the code/opencode/openchamber/nix streams. Every claim response was stamped lane_id=any-h; every checkpoint, block, park, and complete addressed its claim; zero exit-5 "not claimed by repo-worker-code" failures. The 2026-11-11 exit-5 shape did not recur on this surface.
- **The 2026-11-16 "lane mismatch" is pinpointed — it is a client-side vocabulary trap, not broker misattribution.** Three different fields share the word "lane": tasks.lane_id (the claiming lane, e.g. any-n), repo_task_lane_ledger.assigned_lane (the assignment MODE: 'opencode' or 'direct'), and ledger.executed_lane (the execution MODE, same two values). The completion path's --execution.lane takes the MODE, validated client-side in pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/client.rs (execution_arg): any other value dies with "--execution.lane must be 'opencode' or 'direct'". A worker naturally passes its lane id there — exactly what the 2026-11-16 session did — gets rejected, retries with 'opencode', and the ledger then shows executed_lane='opencode' next to a claim stamped any-n: the recorded "mismatch".
- **Deterministic reproduction (2026-11-17, no live task touched):** fleet queue complete 999999999 --execution '{"lane":"any-n"}' dies client-side with that message before any broker call; the same call with '{"lane":"opencode"}' passes validation and reaches the broker (failing only on the nonexistent task). record_execution (turso_queue.rs) stamps executed_lane from this field; lane_family_of (turso_queue.rs:523) is the separate claim-time lane-id parser.
- **What remains for criterion 3:** (1) a fix decision — cheapest correct fix is client-side: rename the error to state the semantics ("--execution.lane is the execution mode: 'opencode' (executed via an opencode session) or 'direct'") and/or accept-and-translate a lane id; a schema-level executed_lane_id is the heavier alternative; (2) a claimed-row snapshot sample from the OpenChamber surface to pair with the Muse sample above. Task 20022 is parked with this pinpoint as its resume state; the issue stays open for Drew's close call per the 2026-11-13 reminder.

- **Fix decision (the parked "client error semantics vs schema executed_lane_id" question): BOTH, split-key.** `--execution.lane` keeps the execution mode (`opencode`|`direct`); the executing lane id is recorded under a new `lane_id` key / ledger column `executed_lane_id`. A lane id passed in `lane` (the 2026-11-16 call shape) is accepted and translated: mode derived from its family (opencode family → `opencode`, else `direct`), id preserved. Mode-only callers are byte-identical to before; garbage still dies, with a message that states the semantics.
- **PR #10961** (branch `queue/20022-7598-execution-lane-id`, commit d09e9be205): client `normalize_execution` in `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/client.rs`; broker `execution_lane_fields` + `record_execution` in `turso_queue.rs` (same split for callers that bypass the client; additive `executed_lane_id` migration in the existing pattern).
